facts.fact: A worker may present a complaint to an employment tribunal that his employer has made a deduction from his wages in contravention of section 13, including a deduction made in contravention of that section as it applies by virtue of section 18(2).
quotes: A worker may present a complaint to an employment tribunal— (a) that his employer has made a deduction from his wages in contravention of section 13 (including a deduction made in contravention of that section as it applies by virtue of section 18(2))

facts.fact: A worker may present a complaint to an employment tribunal that his employer has received from him a payment in contravention of section 15, including a payment received in contravention of that section as it applies by virtue of section 20(1).
quotes: A worker may present a complaint to an employment tribunal—
(b) that his employer has received from him a payment in contravention of section 15 (including a payment received in contravention of that section as it applies by virtue of section 20(1))

facts.fact: A worker may present a complaint to an employment tribunal that his employer has recovered from his wages by means of one or more deductions falling within section 18(1) an amount or aggregate amount exceeding the limit applying to the deduction or deductions under that provision.
quotes: A worker may present a complaint to an employment tribunal—

(c) that his employer has recovered from his wages by means of one or more deductions falling within section 18(1) an amount or aggregate amount exceeding the limit applying to the deduction or deductions under that provision

facts.fact: A worker may present a complaint to an employment tribunal that his employer has received from him in pursuance of one or more demands for payment made on a particular pay day in accordance with section 20, a payment or payments of an amount or aggregate amount exceeding the limit applying to the demand or demands under section 21(1).
quotes: A worker may present a complaint to an employment tribunal—

(d) that his employer has received from him in pursuance of one or more demands for payment made (in accordance with section 20) on a particular pay day, a payment or payments of an amount or aggregate amount exceeding the limit applying to the demand or demands under section 21(1).

facts.fact: Subject to subsection (4), an employment tribunal shall not consider a complaint under this section relating to a deduction by the employer unless it is presented before the end of the period of three months beginning with the date of payment of the wages from which the deduction was made.
quotes: Subject to subsection (4), an employment tribunal shall not consider a complaint under this section unless it is presented before the end of the period of three months beginning with—
(a) in the case of a complaint relating to a deduction by the employer, the date of payment of the wages from which the deduction was made

facts.fact: Subject to subsection (4), an employment tribunal shall not consider a complaint under this section relating to a payment received by the employer unless it is presented before the end of the period of three months beginning with the date when the payment was received.
quotes: Subject to subsection (4), an employment tribunal shall not consider a complaint under this section unless it is presented before the end of the period of three months beginning with—
(b) in the case of a complaint relating to a payment received by the employer, the date when the payment was received.

facts.fact: Where a complaint is brought under this section in respect of a series of deductions or payments, the references in subsection (2) to the deduction or payment are to the last deduction or payment in the series.
quotes: Where a complaint is brought under this section in respect of— (a) a series of deductions or payments
the references in subsection (2) to the deduction or payment are to the last deduction or payment in the series

facts.fact: Where a complaint is brought under this section in respect of a number of payments falling within subsection (1)(d) and made in pursuance of demands for payment subject to the same limit under section 21(1) but received by the employer on different dates, the references in subsection (2) to the deduction or payment are to the last of the payments so received.
quotes: Where a complaint is brought under this section in respect of—

(b) a number of payments falling within subsection (1)(d) and made in pursuance of demands for payment subject to the same limit under section 21(1) but received by the employer on different dates, the references in subsection (2) to the deduction or payment are
to the last of the payments so received.

facts.fact: For a complaint brought in respect of a series of deductions, the period of three months under subsection (2) begins with the date of payment of the wages from which the last deduction in the series was made.
quotes: the references in subsection (2) to the deduction or payment are to the last deduction or payment in the series
period of three months beginning with— (a) in the case of a complaint relating to a deduction by the employer, the date of payment of the wages from which the deduction was made

facts.fact: Section 207B applies for the purposes of subsection (2) to extend time limits to facilitate conciliation before the institution of proceedings.
quotes: Section 207B (extension of time limits to facilitate conciliation before institution of proceedings) applies for the purposes of subsection (2).

facts.fact: The conciliation extension of time limits under Section 207B applies to the period of three months specified in subsection (2) for presenting a complaint.
quotes: Section 207B (extension of time limits to facilitate conciliation before institution of proceedings) applies for the purposes of subsection (2).
period of three months beginning with

facts.fact: Where the employment tribunal is satisfied that it was not reasonably practicable for a complaint under this section to be presented before the end of the relevant period of three months, the tribunal may consider the complaint if it is presented within such further period as the tribunal considers reasonable.
quotes: Where the employment tribunal is satisfied that it was not reasonably practicable for a complaint under this section to be presented before the end of the relevant period of three months, the tribunal may consider the complaint if it is presented within such further period as the tribunal considers reasonable.

facts.fact: Under subsection (4), an employment tribunal may consider a complaint presented within a further period it considers reasonable if presentation within the period of three months was not reasonably practicable.
quotes: Subject to subsection (4), an employment tribunal shall not consider a complaint under this section unless it is presented before the end of the period of three months

Where the employment tribunal is satisfied that it was not reasonably practicable for a complaint under this section to be presented before the end of the relevant period of three months, the tribunal may consider the complaint if it is presented within such further period as the tribunal considers reasonable.

facts.fact: An employment tribunal is not, despite subsections (3) and (4), to consider so much of a complaint brought under this section as relates to a deduction where the date of payment of the wages from which the deduction was made was before the period of two years ending with the date of presentation of the complaint.
quotes: An employment tribunal is not (despite subsections (3) and (4)) to consider so much of a complaint brought under this section as relates to a deduction where the date of payment of the wages from which the deduction was made was before the period of two years ending with the date of presentation of the complaint.

facts.fact: Even where a deduction forms part of a series of deductions under subsection (3), an employment tribunal cannot consider it if the date of wage payment was before the period of two years ending with the complaint presentation date.
quotes: An employment tribunal is not (despite subsections (3) and (4)) to consider so much of a complaint brought under this section as relates to a deduction where the date of payment of the wages from which the deduction was made was before the period of two years ending with the date of presentation of the complaint.
series of deductions

facts.fact: Even where an employment tribunal considers presentation within the period of three months was not reasonably practicable under subsection (4), it cannot consider a deduction where the wage payment date was before the period of two years ending with the date of presentation of the complaint.
quotes: An employment tribunal is not (despite subsections (3) and (4)) to consider so much of a complaint brought under this section as relates to a deduction where the date of payment of the wages from which the deduction was made was before the period of two years ending with the date of presentation of the complaint.
period of three months

facts.fact: Subsection (4A) does not apply so far as a complaint relates to a deduction from wages that are of a kind mentioned in section 27(1)(b) to (j).
quotes: Subsection (4A) does not apply so far as a complaint relates to a deduction from wages that are of a kind mentioned in section 27(1)(b) to (j).

facts.fact: The restriction under subsection (4A) barring consideration of deductions from wages paid before the period of two years ending with presentation of the complaint does not apply to deductions from wages of a kind mentioned in section 27(1)(b) to (j).
quotes: Subsection (4A) does not apply so far as a complaint relates to a deduction from wages that are of a kind mentioned in section 27(1)(b) to (j).
before the period of two years ending with the date of presentation of the complaint.

facts.fact: No complaint shall be presented under this section in respect of any deduction made in contravention of section 86 of the Trade Union and Labour Relations (Consolidation) Act 1992 regarding deduction of political fund contributions where a certificate of exemption or objection has been given.
quotes: No complaint shall be presented under this section in respect of any deduction made in contravention of section 86 of the Trade Union and Labour Relations (Consolidation) Act 1992 (deduction of political fund contribution where certificate of exemption or objection has been given).

facts.fact: Although a worker may present a complaint regarding deductions from wages under section 13, no complaint may be presented under this section in respect of any deduction made in contravention of section 86 of the Trade Union and Labour Relations (Consolidation) Act 1992.
quotes: A worker may present a complaint to an employment tribunal— (a) that his employer has made a deduction from his wages in contravention of section 13
No complaint shall be presented under this section in respect of any deduction made in contravention of section 86 of the Trade Union and Labour Relations (Consolidation) Act 1992

facts.fact: The amount of the basic award shall be calculated subject to the provisions of sections 120 to 122, section 126, and the section itself.
quotes: Subject to the provisions of this section, sections 120 to 122 and section 126, the amount of the basic award shall be calculated

facts.fact: Calculating the amount of the basic award begins by determining the period, ending with the effective date of termination, during which the employee has been continuously employed.
quotes: the amount of the basic award shall be calculated by
determining the period, ending with the effective date of termination, during which the employee has been continuously employed

facts.fact: Calculating the amount of the basic award includes reckoning backwards from the end of the continuous employment period the number of years of employment falling within that period.
quotes: the amount of the basic award shall be calculated by
reckoning backwards from the end of that period the number of years of employment falling within that period

facts.fact: Calculating the amount of the basic award includes allowing the appropriate amount for each reckoned year of employment.
quotes: the amount of the basic award shall be calculated by
allowing the appropriate amount for each of those years of employment

facts.fact: In subsection (1)(c), the appropriate amount means one and a half weeks’ pay for a year of employment in which the employee was not below the age of forty-one.
quotes: In subsection (1)(c) “the appropriate amount” means
one and a half weeks’ pay for a year of employment in which the employee was not below the age of forty-one

facts.fact: In subsection (1)(c), the appropriate amount means one week’s pay for a year of employment not within paragraph (a) in which the employee was not below the age of twenty-two.
quotes: In subsection (1)(c) “the appropriate amount” means
one week’s pay for a year of employment (not within paragraph (a)) in which he was not below the age of twenty-two

facts.fact: In subsection (1)(c), the appropriate amount means half a week’s pay for a year of employment not within paragraph (a) or (b).
quotes: In subsection (1)(c) “the appropriate amount” means
half a week’s pay for a year of employment not within paragraph (a) or (b)

facts.fact: In subsection (1)(c), the appropriate amount means one and a half weeks’ pay for a year of employment in which the employee was aged forty-one or over.
quotes: In subsection (1)(c) “the appropriate amount” means
one and a half weeks’ pay for a year of employment in which the employee was not below the age of forty-one

facts.fact: In subsection (1)(c), the appropriate amount means one week’s pay for a year of employment not within paragraph (a) in which the employee was aged twenty-two or over.
quotes: In subsection (1)(c) “the appropriate amount” means
one week’s pay for a year of employment (not within paragraph (a)) in which he was not below the age of twenty-two

facts.fact: Where twenty years of employment have been reckoned under subsection (1), no account shall be taken under that subsection of any year of employment earlier than those twenty years.
quotes: Where twenty years of employment have been reckoned under subsection (1), no account shall be taken under that subsection of any year of employment earlier than those twenty years

facts.fact: The maximum number of years of employment that can be taken into account under subsection (1) is twenty years.
quotes: Where twenty years of employment have been reckoned under subsection (1), no account shall be taken under that subsection of any year of employment earlier than those twenty years

facts.fact: When a worker begins employment with an employer, the employer must give the worker a written statement of particulars of employment.
quotes: Where a worker begins employment with an employer, the employer shall give to the worker a written statement of particulars of employment.

facts.fact: Subject to sections 2(2) to (4), the particulars required by subsections (3) and (4) must be included in a single document.
quotes: Subject to sections 2(2) to (4)— (a) the particulars required by subsections (3) and (4) must be included in a single document;

facts.fact: Subject to sections 2(2) to (4), the statement of employment particulars must be given not later than the beginning of the employment.
quotes: Subject to sections 2(2) to (4)—
the statement must be given not later than the beginning of the employment.

facts.fact: Subject to sections 2(2) to (4), the statement containing the names of the employer and worker, start date, and the particulars required by subsection (4) must be given as a single document.
quotes: Subject to sections 2(2) to (4)— (a) the particulars required by subsections (3) and (4) must be included in a single document;
the names of the employer and worker, (b) the date when the employment began

facts.fact: The statement of employment particulars must contain particulars of the names of the employer and worker.
quotes: The statement shall contain particulars of— (a) the names of the employer and worker,

facts.fact: The statement of employment particulars must contain particulars of the date when the employment began.
quotes: The statement shall contain particulars of—
the date when the employment began

facts.fact: In the case of a statement given to an employee, the statement must contain particulars of the date on which the employee’s period of continuous employment began, taking into account any employment with a previous employer which counts towards that period.
quotes: The statement shall contain particulars of—

in the case of a statement given to an employee, the date on which the employee’s period of continuous employment began (taking into account any employment with a previous employer which counts towards that period).

facts.fact: The statement of employment particulars must contain particulars of the scale or rate of remuneration or the method of calculating remuneration.
quotes: The statement shall also contain particulars
the scale or rate of remuneration or the method of calculating remuneration,

facts.fact: The statement of employment particulars must contain particulars of the intervals at which remuneration is paid, such as weekly, monthly or other specified intervals.
quotes: The statement shall also contain particulars
the intervals at which remuneration is paid (that is, weekly, monthly or other specified intervals),

facts.fact: The statement of employment particulars must contain particulars of any terms and conditions relating to hours of work, including normal working hours, required days of the week, and whether and how such hours or days may be variable.
quotes: The statement shall also contain particulars

any terms and conditions relating to hours of work including any terms and conditions relating to— (i) normal working hours, (ii) the days of the week the worker is required to work, and (iii) whether or not such hours or days may be variable, and if they may be how they vary or how that variation is to be determined.

facts.fact: The statement of employment particulars must contain particulars of any terms and conditions relating to entitlement to holidays, including public holidays, and holiday pay, sufficient to enable precise calculation of entitlement including accrued holiday pay on termination.
quotes: The statement shall also contain particulars

any terms and conditions relating to any of the following— (i) entitlement to holidays, including public holidays, and holiday pay (the particulars given being sufficient to enable the worker’s entitlement, including any entitlement to accrued holiday pay on the termination of employment, to be precisely calculated),

facts.fact: The statement of employment particulars must contain particulars of any terms and conditions relating to incapacity for work due to sickness or injury, including any provision for sick pay.
quotes: The statement shall also contain particulars
incapacity for work due to sickness or injury, including any provision for sick pay,

facts.fact: The statement of employment particulars must contain particulars of any terms and conditions relating to any other paid leave.
quotes: The statement shall also contain particulars
any other paid leave,

facts.fact: The statement of employment particulars must contain particulars of any terms and conditions relating to pensions and pension schemes.
quotes: The statement shall also contain particulars
pensions and pension schemes,

facts.fact: The statement of employment particulars must contain particulars of any other benefits provided by the employer that do not fall within another paragraph of the subsection.
quotes: The statement shall also contain particulars
any other benefits provided by the employer that do not fall within another paragraph of this subsection,

facts.fact: The statement of employment particulars must contain particulars of the length of notice which the worker is obliged to give and entitled to receive to terminate the contract of employment or other worker’s contract.
quotes: The statement shall also contain particulars
the length of notice which the worker is obliged to give and entitled to receive to terminate his contract of employment or other worker’s contract,

facts.fact: The statement of employment particulars must contain particulars of the title of the job which the worker is employed to do or a brief description of the work for which the worker is employed.
quotes: The statement shall also contain particulars
the title of the job which the worker is employed to do or a brief description of the work for which he is employed,

facts.fact: Where the employment is not intended to be permanent, the statement of employment particulars must contain particulars of the period for which it is expected to continue or, if for a fixed term, the date when it is to end.
quotes: The statement shall also contain particulars
where the employment is not intended to be permanent, the period for which it is expected to continue or, if it is for a fixed term, the date when it is to end,

facts.fact: The statement of employment particulars must contain particulars of any probationary period, including any conditions and its duration.
quotes: The statement shall also contain particulars
any probationary period, including any conditions and its duration,

facts.fact: The statement of employment particulars must contain particulars of either the place of work or, where the worker is required or permitted to work at various places, an indication of that and of the address of the employer.
quotes: The statement shall also contain particulars
either the place of work or, where the worker is required or permitted to work at various places, an indication of that and of the address of the employer,

facts.fact: The statement of employment particulars must contain particulars of any collective agreements which directly affect the terms and conditions of the employment, including the persons by whom they were made where the employer is not a party.
quotes: The statement shall also contain particulars
any collective agreements which directly affect the terms and conditions of the employment including, where the employer is not a party, the persons by whom they were made,

facts.fact: Where the worker is required to work outside the United Kingdom for a period of more than one month, the statement of employment particulars must contain particulars of the period of work outside the United Kingdom, the currency of remuneration, additional remuneration and benefits, and return terms and conditions.
quotes: The statement shall also contain particulars

where the worker is required to work outside the United Kingdom for a period of more than one month— (i) the period for which he is to work outside the United Kingdom, (ii) the currency in which remuneration is to be paid while he is working outside the United Kingdom, (iii) any additional remuneration payable to him, and any benefits to be provided to or in respect of him, by reason of his being required to work outside the United Kingdom, and (iv) any terms and conditions relating to his return to the United Kingdom.

facts.fact: The statement of employment particulars must contain particulars of any training entitlement provided by the employer.
quotes: The statement shall also contain particulars
any training entitlement provided by the employer,

facts.fact: The statement of employment particulars must contain particulars of any part of the training entitlement which the employer requires the worker to complete.
quotes: The statement shall also contain particulars
any part of that training entitlement which the employer requires the worker to complete,

facts.fact: The statement of employment particulars must contain particulars of any other training which the employer requires the worker to complete and which the employer will not bear the cost of.
quotes: The statement shall also contain particulars
any other training which the employer requires the worker to complete and which the employer will not bear the cost of.

facts.fact: The statement of employment particulars must contain particulars, including conditions and duration, of any temporary period specified in the contract commencing at the beginning of employment to enable the employer to assess the worker's suitability for the employment.
quotes: any probationary period, including any conditions and its duration,

“probationary period” means a temporary period specified in the contract of employment or other worker’s contract between a worker and an employer that— (a) commences at the beginning of the employment, and (b) is intended to enable the employer to assess the worker’s suitability for the employment.

facts.fact: The requirement to include terms and conditions relating to pensions and pension schemes does not apply to a worker of a body or authority if the worker’s pension rights depend on the terms of a pension scheme established under an Act, and the provision requires the body or authority to give the new worker information concerning those rights or determination of questions affecting them.
quotes: Subsection (4)(d)(iii) does not apply to a worker of a body or authority if— (a) the worker’s pension rights depend on the terms of a pension scheme established under any provision contained in or having effect under any Act, and (b) any such provision requires the body or authority to give to a new worker information concerning the worker’s pension rights or the determination of questions affecting those rights.

facts.fact: A body or authority is not required to provide particulars of pensions and pension schemes in the statement of employment particulars if statutory provisions require it to inform new workers about their pension rights under an Act-established scheme.
quotes: Subsection (4)(d)(iii) does not apply to a worker of a body or authority if— (a) the worker’s pension rights depend on the terms of a pension scheme established under any provision contained in or having effect under any Act, and (b) any such provision requires the body or authority to give to a new worker information concerning the worker’s pension rights or the determination of questions affecting those rights.
pensions and pension schemes,

facts.fact: A probationary period is defined as a temporary period specified in the contract of employment or other worker’s contract between a worker and an employer that commences at the beginning of the employment and is intended to enable the employer to assess the worker’s suitability for the employment.
quotes: In this section “probationary period” means a temporary period specified in the contract of employment or other worker’s contract between a worker and an employer that— (a) commences at the beginning of the employment, and (b) is intended to enable the employer to assess the worker’s suitability for the employment.
